newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK housing block fire kills three, injures six.
newsitem.headline: HK housing block fire kills three, injures six.

text.p: Three people died and six, including a fireman, were injured on Friday in a fire in a Hong Kong residential building caused by a suspected arson attack, officials said.

The blaze, latest in a series of deadly fires in the territory, broke out early in the morning on the first floor of a ramshackle four-storey building in Shau Kei Wan on the eastern end of Hong Kong island, officials said.
At the height of the fire, which took about an hour and a half to extinguish, flames engulfed the building.
Senior superintendent Gregory Lam told reporters police suspected the fire was an arson attack and had detained a 36-year-old woman in the building for questioning. No charges were made.
Lam said there were traces of petrol outside the door of a flat where the fire was thought to have started, and the apartment's iron gate was chained from the outside.
Lam said firemen found the bodies of three men inside the flat. Two seriously injured men were also there.
Hong Kong has suffered some of its worst fires in recent months.

Earlier in April, a fire believed to have been caused by a cigarette butt swept through a residential block in the Mei Foo district of the Kowloon Peninsula, killing nine people, including two babies, and injuring about 36.
In January a karaoke bar fire, blamed on an arson attack, killed 17 people in Kowloon's Tsimshatsui entertainment district.
Last November, a fire in a commercial building in Kowloon's Nathan Road tourist shopping mecca killed 39 people and injured 81. It was Hong Kong's worst building fire on record.
